statements.impact_statement: EXAMPLE ONLY — this statement is a template and names a fabricated advisory id, so it must never be copied into security/atif-sql.openvex.json unchanged. It exists to show the shape and the required DEPTH of argument: name the single reachability path, the measurement that closes it, the date, and the condition that would reopen it. A real statement at this depth would read: jinja2 reaches this workspace on exactly one path, harbor -> jinja2, and atif-sql never renders a template — `atif-sql` has no template surface at all, and the only jinja2 import in the closure is harbor's own prompt rendering, which atif-converter does not call because it enters harbor through `ClaudeCode._convert_events_to_trajectory` and nothing below it touches `Environment` or `Template`. Measured 2026-08-28: a module-load probe over the full 816-test suite recorded zero imports of `jinja2.Environment`, positive-controlled against a forced import first; and the advisory's vulnerable code path requires an attacker-supplied template string, which no atif-sql entry point accepts because every input is a Claude Code transcript already on local disk. Revisit if a future analyze/report pipeline renders templates from corpus content, which is what would put attacker-influenced text into a template source.
